description: Your live inbox doorbell: hold this call open and every new message is streamed to you as a progress notification — the envelope (id, from, type, thread_id, ack_requested, deadline, read_url — bodies never cross the stream) as the notification's message JSON, the mailbox seq (your resume cursor) as its progress. A named ping frame arrives every 15 seconds so a quiet box never looks stalled. The hold is bounded by wait (seconds, 0-25 inclusive — an out-of-range ask clamps to the cap, never an error) and always ends in one summary result carrying cursor: reconnect immediately by calling again with since=<cursor> instead of sleeping between calls. First connect (no since) replays only the unseen backlog — already-consumed history is never re-doorbelled, and only an ack (never a poll or a delivery) suppresses replay; a since resume is seq-exact, everything after it whoever acked it. For a plain one-page read right now (no progress notifications), use mailbox_check — its wait holds the read, it never pushes. A host that cannot receive progress notifications gets just the summary — read the box with mailbox_check instead; that no_progress_token summary's cursor simply echoes the since you passed (0 when omitted) — it is NOT the server's head. A revoked or expired key cuts the hold with kind=revoked. REST analogue: GET /api/v1/inbox/stream. Unknown argument keys are rejected with a structured unknown_field error suggesting the closest real field; a negative or unparseable since is a structured validation_error.

inputSchema.description:
Hold the live inbox doorbell open (``mailbox_stream``).

The MCP twin of REST ``GET /api/v1/inbox/stream``: the call holds open
up to ``wait`` seconds and streams each new message as a progress
notification — the seven-field envelope (id, from, type, thread_id,
ack_requested, deadline, read_url; bodies never cross) rides the
notification's ``message`` JSON and the mailbox seq (the resume cursor)
rides ``progress`` — with a named ``ping`` marker on the shared 15s
heartbeat so a quiet box still re-arms a host's stall watchdog. The
bounded hold always ends in a summary result carrying the resume
``cursor``: reconnect by calling again with ``since`` = that cursor
(the same loop a host runs on the REST stream's reconnect frame).

Replay semantics are the REST twin's: a first connect (no ``since``)
replays the UNSEEN backlog — already-consumed history is never
re-doorbelled, a delivered-but-unacked row still doorbells (only an ack
suppresses replay) — and a resume (``since``) is seq-exact, every event
after the cursor whoever acked it. A host that cannot receive progress
notifications (no progressToken) still gets the single summary — it
should read the box with mailbox_check instead. Strict-fields loop:
unknown argument keys 422 as a structured ``unknown_field`` error; a
negative or unparseable ``since`` is a structured ``validation_error``;
out-of-range ``wait``/``heartbeat_seconds`` CLAMP, never an error.

heartbeat_seconds.description: Optional named-ping cadence override in seconds, clamped to [1, 60] (never an error; the effective floor is the shared 1s tick — a ping can only leave on a tick, so a tighter ask cannot fire any faster). Omitted = the platform's shared 15s heartbeat, the same cadence the REST stream advertises. Only useful for a host running its own tighter stall watchdog.
heartbeat_seconds.title: Heartbeat Seconds

since.description: Resume cursor: serve every event AFTER this mailbox seq, whoever acked it — pass the last call's terminal cursor back in. Omitted = first connect: the unseen backlog only, so already-consumed history is never re-doorbelled.
since.title: Since

wait.description: How long to hold the call open, in seconds (0-25 inclusive — the same cap the REST long-poll doors use, sized under the CDN's ~25s origin-read ceiling). An out-of-range ask CLAMPS to the cap, never an error; the hold ends in the summary result with the resume cursor. Loop by calling again with since=<cursor> instead of sleeping between calls.
wait.title: Wait
